findings.title: Default value timezone.now() is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` a single time when the class is defined at module import, so every AssignmentSource constructed without an explicit `queued` value gets the same stale timestamp (the process import time) rather than the time the source was created. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to get a per-instance timestamp.

findings.title: datetime in AssignmentSource.to_dict() will fail Celery JSON serialization
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound passes `assignment_source.to_dict()` (which includes the `queued` datetime) as the `assignment_source_dict` kwarg to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`. Sentry's Celery tasks are serialized with JSON, and a raw datetime is not JSON-serializable, so enqueueing the task will raise a serialization error (or kombu EncodeError) whenever an assignment originated from an inbound integration webhook — the exact path this PR adds. The datetime should be serialized to an ISO string (and parsed back in from_dict) or the field omitted from the task payload.

findings.title: should_sync is now always called with a second positional argument; existing overrides with the old signature will raise TypeError
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`. Only the base classes in this PR were updated to accept the new parameter; any concrete integration installation that overrides `should_sync(self, attribute)` (a common pattern for Jira/VSTS/Azure DevOps-style integrations) will raise `TypeError: should_sync() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`, and since the task retries on unexpected exceptions, this will burn retries on every assignee sync for those providers. Callers should pass the source as a keyword and overrides need to be audited/updated, or the call should be made defensively.
